title: Non-communicable disease prevention in aging societies
bottleneck: As populations age, the disease burden shifts to non-communicable diseases (cardiovascular, cancer, diabetes, dementia) that share aging itself as the dominant risk factor, yet research funding and health systems remain organized disease-by-disease. Prevention science is dwarfed by treatment spending, and the geroscience hypothesis (target aging to prevent many diseases at once) has no regulatory or funding home.
why_it_blocks: Treating diseases one at a time in an aging population is a losing strategy: curing one leaves the patient exposed to the next. Without a prevention paradigm built around aging, healthspan gains will always lag lifespan gains.
current_state: WHO and national strategies acknowledge NCDs but fund them in silos. The TAME trial (metformin for aging) aims to create a regulatory precedent for targeting aging, with results expected late 2020s.

sources.title: Bottlenecks in aging research (Lifespan.io researcher survey)
